subject: Proposed sentinel-based success criteria & rollback playbook for HealthLytics evaluation
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed sentinel-based success criteria & rollback playbook for HealthLytics evaluation

Samira —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As promised, attached is a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on measurable "sentinels" we can monitor during your 30-day evaluation window, plus a short rollback/playbook that defines exit gates and acceptance tests. High-level items: 

- Success sentinels (what we measure):
  - End-to-end latency at 95th percentile <= 350ms for 1k concurrent sessions
  - Semantic accuracy (domain eval set) F1 >= 0.84 across the 120-case prompt suite
  - No data exfiltration flags; KMS key usage audited to match your KMS policy
  - Cost per 1k tokens under the committed pilot baseline (budget trigger)

- Exit gates (hard stops):
  - Any security audit failure flagged by your SOC engineer (blocker)
  - Sustained 95th-latency breaches over 4 hours during business hours
  - Reproducible semantic failures causing >5% incorrect classification on high-risk prompts

- Acceptance tests (what we run together):
  - Production-like load test (script + dataset) — pass/fail defined in attached acceptance-tests.yml
  - 3 stakeholder sign-offs (DataOps, ProdSec, Clinical SME)
  - Final demo with recorded transcript and shared evaluation notebook

I've also added a lightweight rollback playbook: if any exit gate is triggered we fail to canary and revert traffic to the pre-pilot endpoint, notify stakeholders, and spin up a post-mortem within 48 hours.

See attached MAP_v2.xlsx (timeline + owners) and acceptance-tests.yml for the pass/fail thresholds. Proposed next steps:
1) Your teams confirm owner names for DataOps and ProdSec by Wednesday (24th).
2) We schedule the production-like load run on 06/30 (will need a 2-hour maintenance window).
3) Final demo + sign-off call on 07/02.

If that aligns, I'll lock the timeline and open the HubSpot mutual action plan so we both have visibility.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina.h@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0179

Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP timeline + owners, 1 sheet)
Attachment: acceptance-tests.yml (test suite and thresholds)
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@healthlytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthLytics Procurement <procurement@healthlytics.com>, Kiran Shah <kiran.shah@healthlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed sentinel-based success criteria & rollback playbook for HealthLytics evaluation

Thanks, Mina — this looks actionable and tighter than the prior MAP draft (appreciate the focus on sentinels). Quick notes from our side: 

- I can confirm Kiran (DataOps) and I (Product Owner) will be owners. I'll check ProdSec owners — tagging procurement so they can align on any procurement/ops constraints.
- We have an internal policy that requires a second SME sign-off for clinical prompts that involve PHI risk. Can we add a chapter to the acceptance-tests.yml that enumerates PHI-sensitive prompts and the remediation for false positives?
- Regarding the cost trigger: propose we set a soft alert at 120% of baseline and a hard stop at 150% for the pilot.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you share the exact load-test script you plan to use? We need to validate against our traffic replay tool.
2) If exit gate is triggered during the weekend, what's the automated fallback?

Samira
Director, Product — HealthLytics
samira.k@healthlytics.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed sentinel-based success criteria & rollback playbook for HealthLytics evaluation

Samira —

Great notes. Answers below and edits attached: 

- PHI-sensitive prompt handling: added a PHI appendix in acceptance-tests.yml (lines 72-120) that lists the sensitive prompt categories, expected redaction behavior, and remediation steps. We'll run those prompts under a masked dataset in your environment; no PHI leaves your VPC.

- Cost triggers: updated MAP_v2.xlsx to show soft alert at 120% and hard stop at 150% with notify+escalate steps.

- Load-test script: attaching demo-recording-0623.mp4 (recording of the script run) and the load script URL inside the Drive folder — script uses ramp-to-peak with randomized user seeds to mimic session churn. Link is in the Drive doc.

- Weekend fallback: the platform will automatically failover to the pre-pilot model variant and route new sessions to the previously pinned endpoint. We'll open a PagerDuty incident to your oncall ProdSec contact if the hard stop occurs; we can make that immediate or delayed per your preference (default: immediate).

Proposed timeline updates (attached MAP_v2.xlsx):
- 06/30: Production-like load run (owner: Kiran Shah)
- 07/01: Analysis & bug fix sprint (if needed)
- 07/02: Final demo + signoffs (Product + DataOps + ProdSec)

If okay, I'll update the HubSpot MAP and loop in your procurement contact for the MOU.

Thanks — Mina

Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (updated with cost triggers & owners)
Attachment: demo-recording-0623.mp4 (short recording of the load script)
From: Kiran Shah <kiran.shah@healthlytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed sentinel-based success criteria & rollback playbook for HealthLytics evaluation

+1 on the PHI appendix — this is critical. A couple of implementation notes from DataOps: 

- We will run the load test in a mirrored staging cluster (same infra characteristics) and replay 48 hours worth of traffic compressed into a 2-hour window. Expect synthetic session churn and periodic bulk uploads.
- For the weekend fallback, please confirm that KV cache invalidation will occur on failover — we cannot serve stale results for clinical lookups.

Can the Redwood team confirm cache invalidation will be part of the failover playbook? If yes, we can sign off on the timeline and owners.

Kiran
Sr. Data Engineer — HealthLytics
From: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.com>
To: Kiran Shah <kiran.shah@healthlytics.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, HealthLytics Procurement <procurement@healthlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed sentinel-based success criteria & rollback playbook for HealthLytics evaluation

Kiran —

Confirmed: KV cache invalidation is included in the automated failover sequence. Sequence summary: 1) Pause routing to canary; 2) Flush KV caches tied to clinical namespaces; 3) Failover traffic to pinned endpoint; 4) Send incident notification & open a joint ticket. We have the invalidation script parameterized by namespace so we can target clinical namespaces only.

Action items: 
- Samira: confirm ProdSec owner for weekend POC by EOD 06/24 so we can add them to the PagerDuty integration.
- Kiran: confirm staging cluster availability for 06/30 load run (2-hour window).
- Procurement: please review the MOU we pushed to your HubSpot record and confirm any procurement gating items.

Once we have those confirmations, I'll mark the MAP as "locked" in HubSpot and we can proceed with the run.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting this into a short pilot and driving to sign-off.

— Mina
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina.h@redwood.com
